MX17 response simulation · det3 cosmics, 490 V · 2026-10-18

The simulation now matches det3 in amplitude and strip extent at every angle; what is left is the peak strip of inclined Y tracks and the neighbour timing

Six days ago it was ×1.6–2.4 too dim and 70 ns too slow. Two physics additions (fast hydrocarbon ions, avalanche feedback), six bug fixes, the measured drift column (26.5 mm, not 30) and a joint gain refit closed that. Slides 9–13 are new on 10-17/18. None of the tuning has been tested on a second gas or chamber.

Details

Target run: det3 cosmic bench, Ar/iC4H10 95/5, 490 V mesh, 1000 V drift over 30 mm, the June 27 long run (long_run_resist_490V_drift_1000V). Data are selected by the true angle of the M3 reference track, with no det3 reco or quality cut; the sim takes all events at its fixed angle (FRESH_LOOK §18.2).

The previous state, with the six open discrepancies, is the 2026-10-12 note. The full record is MX17_Geant/design/report/FRESH_LOOK_2026-10-12.md §8–20.

Details

Each stage is a separate code: Geant4 (mm_sim) → Stage A clusters → Stage B digitiser (response/digitizer: drift, mesh, avalanche sampling, ion signal, induction kernels) → Stage C DREAM/FEU (response/dream) → sim_decoded_*.root → the same wft reconstruction as the data.

The offline inputs (gas table, transparency, avalanche calibration, kernels) are computed once by Magboltz, Garfield++ and COMSOL. Per event, only Geant4 and the sampling run.

Details

"Closed" means within the pre-registered band on the target run. It does not mean tested on a second run: the ion speed, the feedback bG and the shaper were all read from this same run (slide 13).

The gain slope is "explained" rather than "closed": the feedback model fitted to the shape of the June HV ladder gives both the slope and the amplitude with one parameter, but the decisive test (a ladder at a second isobutane fraction) needs bench time.

Amplitude: two physics additions took the sim from ×2 too dim to the data

Peak-strip median, data ÷ sim, vertical tracks, data by true M3 angle. Each point adds one change.

X (FEU 7)

Y (FEU 8)

A hydrocarbon ion makes the pulse faster, so more of the charge reaches the peak: ×1.2.

Feedback multiplies the gain by 1/(1 − bG) ≈ ×1.8. bG was fitted to the shape of the HV ladder, not to this amplitude.

The corrected primaries (−9 %) then over-shoot at bG 0.45, so bG moves up to 0.47.

det3 June 27 long run, 490 V; data |view angle| < 3°, |other| < 6°, fiducial M3 box; sim 3000 events per angle.

The joint optimum is bG ≈ 0.47, a small step from verdict 1's 0.45. The pre-registration said 0.49–0.53: the amplitude falls faster with bG than predicted.

Pulse shape: the physical ion mobility reproduces the fitted one within 6 ns

Median 10–90 % rise of the peak strip, sim − data, inclined tracks. Ion rebuilt from Garfield birth heights in the mesh field map, at three mobilities.

Ar⁺, 180 ns (Aug default)

K0 is the reduced mobility in cm²/(V·s). Verdict 1 compressed the Ar⁺ template ×1.75; that matches K0 ≈ 2.2.

The literature value K0 2.05 is 5–6 ns slower than verdict 1. The rise is already +8…+16 ns over the data, so that costs a little agreement for a physical parameter.

Adopted 2026-10-18: K0 2.05 is the v3 default, with 1.80 / 2.25 as the systematic.

Details

Pre-registered in scripts/condor/stageBC_w2_rho5M.sub: Y/X rises 20–50 % and the Y-wing and Y/X interpolations agree within a factor 1.5 in ρ_s. Falsifier: they disagree by more, or Y/X moves < 10 %. The charge sum f agrees to ≤ 0.02, so nothing that scales a whole view (strip C, protection charge division, FEU gain) causes Y/X.

det3 gives f = 0.484 on FEU 7/8 and 0.481–0.494 on FEU 3/4: the FEUs are excluded too. Y pedestal noise is 1.7 % above X, where a strip-C division would make it ~25 % quieter.

What is off is the peak strip: inclined Y keeps too little of its charge on one strip.

A capacitive coupling between neighbouring strips closes the neighbour's leading edge and a third of its delay

Each neighbour gets k·i + τ·di/dt of the central current and the central loses the same. Vertical tracks, event-aligned on the central strip (condor 4480073).

off (v3)

k 0.03, τ 10 ns

k 0.05, τ 15 ns

k 0.06, τ 20 ns

data

At k 0.05, τ 15 ns the neighbour's leading edge goes 0.17 → 0.23 (data 0.22), and the shape rms falls 39 % in X, 13 % in Y.

The rest of the delay is the chain neighbour staying high after its peak: that is the resistive-layer spread, so ρ_s and coupling now need fitting together.

τ = R·C_c = 15 ns (e.g. 300 Ω × 50 pF) is plausible but unmeasured: a candidate, not yet in the baseline. With it on, bG refits to 0.47.

13

Details

--strip-coupling K,TAU_NS (response/dream/coupling.py), on the induced currents before the shaper. Pre-registered in scratchpad/2026-10-18/stageBC_w3_coupling.sub from an offline emulation; falsifier (X delay stays ≥ +115 ns, or rms improves < 10 %) not triggered. The Y rms improvement missed its 20–35 % band (FRESH_LOOK §21.8).

Side effects: amplitude +2…+4 %, the X 20° rise −4 ns, the Y FWHM excess 14 → 9 ns.

ρ_s 2 MΩ/sq shortens the delay a further 15–30 ns but widens the vertical Y profile to 1.05 mm (data 0.85) and overshoots the ±1/central in Y (0.46 vs 0.41): ρ_s cannot close the delay without breaking the Y wings (condor 4480075, §21.11). The remaining prompt share is not the insulator (the August d_k scan moves it < 1 %) nor diffusion (the vertical width is already slightly wide): it points back at the input network.

The mesh transparency was 4 % low, but correcting it changes the signal by only 0.7 %

Garfield single electrons through the woven-mesh map, default vs null-collision stepping, 56 slices, 6400 seeds each (condor 4474926).

With default stepping, electrons jump past field gradients at the wires and are lost: ε = 0.956. Null-collision steps give 0.993, as the G7 check predicted.

The rescued electrons pass close to the wires and come with smaller avalanches, so the gain per surviving electron drops 3 %.

The chain thins by ε, then draws the gain: the product is what matters, and it moves ×1.007. No bG refit is needed.

Details

Pre-registered in mx17_aval_nc1.sub: survival 0.990–0.997 (observed 0.9928, passes) and gain|survived within ±3 % of 24 094 (observed ×0.970, on the edge, about 2.5σ).

Pooled file: EOS response_sim/avalanche/aval_calib_meshfield_nc1_pooled.json (scratchpad/2026-10-16/pool_nc1.py). The chain still runs the nc0 file.

On lxplus this campaign first failed completely: the LCG_109 view ships its own Garfield headers, and ROOT built our classes from them (ComponentGrid 688 vs 720 bytes), which corrupted memory. Fixed in setup_garfield.sh; a same-setup rerun of an August calibration agrees within 1.4σ.

Six bugs and biases were found by checking the chain, not by tuning it

Each one changed what the comparison said. Hover a card for the source.

271→5.7

Common-mode noise [ADC]

Railed events inflated σ_cm 50×, making fake hits and wrong multiplicity.

−11 %

Primary ionisation

Wrong gas densities, W value and missing PAI in Geant4 Stage A.

0.955→0.993

Mesh transparency

A Garfield stepping artefact (slide 9).

688≠720

lxplus Garfield [bytes]

ROOT read the wrong headers; jobs crashed or hung. August results check out.

0 → 1.6 %

Mesh-map inactive region

The lxplus Garfield lacked the region-flag patch: electrons crossed the wires.

None of these is a tuning parameter. Before them the Y amplitude was biased by a third and the multiplicity rows were noise artefacts; after them the comparison can be trusted at the 5–10 % level.

16

Details

The inclined-Y deficit shows most cleanly in the saturated fraction: X rails as often in the sim as in the data at every angle, but inclined Y tracks rail 0.33 of the time in the data and 0.16–0.22 in the sim (§21.9).

The low-side width: the data p25/p50 ratio is lower than the sim's, so the data are broader on the low side. bG hardly changes that (§18.7), which points to something the sim does not have, such as gain varying across the chamber.

17

Details

Dropped since 10-17: the strip-capacitance and FEU-gain ideas. Both scale a whole view, and the X/Y charge sums agree (f within 0.02, and det3 gives the same f on two FEU pairs).

Applying Irakli's −10 % ADC/fC would raise the needed gain, so bG goes up to ~0.50; it changes no shape row.

What this does not rule out, and what needs deciding

Not ruled out

One run. The ion speed, bG and the shaper were all read from the det3 490 V long run. Agreement here is a fit, not a prediction, until a second gas or chamber is checked.

The gain scale. ADC/fC is a datasheet chain; a 10 % error moves bG, not the shape.

Wet gas. The table is dry; the drift speed says the gas may not be (×0.77 gain if wet, §12.2).

Feedback is a model. G/(1 − bG) fits; the carrier (photons) is the leading candidate, not a measurement.

Decisions

Taken 10-17/18: ρ_s 5 MΩ/sq, a 26.5 mm column for det3, the K0 2.05 ion, bG 0.45 (recipes/det3_v3.args).

Adopt the inter-strip coupling (k 0.05, τ 15 ns) as a fitted electronics term, or wait for Irakli's protection values?

Spend the next kernel build on an anisotropic ρ_s (along vs across the stripes)?
